newsitem.title: USA: Ill. bill would disclose names of muni bond buyers.
newsitem.headline: Ill. bill would disclose names of muni bond buyers.

text.p: An Illinois lawmaker is calling for legislation that would require the disclosure of names and addresses of anyone who buys any state debt.
"It's only appropriate that the public be fully informed of who is participating and benefitting from such transactions," said State Rep. Jeff Schoenberg, D-Evanston,

Schoenberg's bill, which is pending before the House Appropriations Committee, which he chairs, would require the state comptroller to compile and maintain a list of names and addresses of all persons and entities that buy any type of state debt.
The list, which would detail the amount of debt owned by each bondholder, would be available for public review upon request as well as through the Internet, according to the bill.

Schoenberg said his bill was mainly aimed at what he called "more obscure" state debt transactions, hinting that some deals may be "politically wired." He said the only way to find out if people behind the deals were buying the deals was to have disclosure of all bond buyers.
"Someone in the deal might have bought the deal conceiveably," he said. "We won't know until we have full disclosure."
Mike Colsch, Illinois deputy budget director, declined to comment on the bill until he had a chance to review it.

Pen Pendleton, a spokesman for the Public Securities Association, called the bill "highly unusual." He said the organization was not aware of any state requiring disclosure of retail and institutional investors in public debt.
Schoenberg's bill would also require disclosure in the case of certificates of participation only of the project funded with the proceeds.

He is one of a group of Democrats from the Illinois House who filed a lawsuit last year challenging the legality of $19.2 million of insured COPs that were sold for a state public aid department building in downtown Chicago.
